description: I am a first-year AI & Data Science student passionate about AI, innovation, and solving real-world problems. I enjoy participating in hackathons, building impactful projects, and continuously learning new technologies. I'm excited to be part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge to collaborate, learn, and contribute meaningful solutions.
summary: We built a crop-rotation decision-support tool that helps farmers choose rotations that protect soil, conserve water and withstand a changing climate. A farmer drops a pin on their field and sets priorities such as soil health, water conservation, profit, drought resilience and erosion control. The tool pulls live data at runtime: NASA POWER weather, GLDAS and SMAP soil moisture, IMERG rainfall, MODIS/VIIRS and Landsat vegetation indices, ECOSTRESS heat and water stress, and SRTM terrain. It combines these with USDA soil data, Cropland Data Layer rotation history and local climate records. From this it builds a field condition profile, scores candidate crops and multi-year rotations against a sourced crop knowledge base, and tests them under drier, hotter and late-frost scenarios. Each recommendation explains why, cites its data sources and fetch times, and shows a confidence score that drops when data are missing. Farmers worldwide face drought, heat and declining soils, and a poor rotation choice is costly. By turning NASA Earth observations into plain-language, field-specific guidance, the tool makes long-term resilience decisions easier and evidence-based.
details:
How It Works

AgroAdapt AI is an end-to-end agricultural decision-support platform that turns satellite telemetry and soil chemistry into actionable, multi-season planting schedules:

  1. Interactive Satellite Parcel Selection: Farmers drop a pin or search any farm location on an interactive hybrid satellite map, specifying parcel size, irrigation setup, and primary farming goals (profit maximization, water conservation, or soil regeneration).
  2. Automated Multi-Sensor Environmental Telemetry: Using the selected coordinates, the system queries live agroclimatology, soil moisture, rainfall reliability, vegetation vigor, land-surface thermal stress, and terrain slope datasets.
  3. Agronomic Scoring & 3-Season Sequence Engine: A multi-criteria matching model evaluates local water availability, thermal risk, and soil parameters (pH, organic carbon, NPK, texture) to compute a prominent Rotation Match Score alongside an optimized 3-season crop sequence (such as a cereal–legume–cereal rotation), 3 alternative rotation blocks, and a Top 5 individual crop leaderboard.
  4. Interactive Crop-Swapping & Financial Simulation: Farmers can swap individual crops within any season to see real-time recalculations of soil nitrogen balance, irrigation savings, pest-cycle interruption, and net profit across four global currencies ($ USD, ₹ INR, € EUR, and ¥ JPY).

Key Benefits

  • Natural Soil Fertility Restoration: Prioritizes nitrogen-fixing legumes in rotation cycles to replenish soil organic matter and reduce synthetic fertilizer dependency.
  • Water & Drought Resilience: Matches crop water requirements against historical rainfall reliability and root-zone moisture to minimize crop failure during dry spells.
  • Pest & Disease Cycle Interruption: Breaks host-specific pathogen and weed cycles by alternating crop families across consecutive seasons.
  • Financial Clarity Across Markets: Translates agronomic yield estimates into clear net return projections in multiple currencies, helping growers compare economic trade-offs before planting.
  • Zero-Barrier Accessibility: Eliminates scientific jargon by converting complex Earth-observation metrics into plain-language Farmer Q&A insights and visual scorecards.

Intended Impact

Continuous monocropping and unpredictable weather patterns degrade topsoil, deplete groundwater, and threaten smallholder livelihoods worldwide. AgroAdapt AI aims to democratize space-agency climate intelligence and precision agronomy—giving everyday farmers, agricultural extension workers, and rural cooperatives free, instant access to tools previously limited to large commercial agribusinesses. Over multiple harvest cycles, widespread adoption supports higher net farm incomes, lower chemical runoff, improved carbon sequestration, and long-term food security.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used

  • Frontend & Application Logic: React (Hooks, Memoized Agronomic Scoring Engine), JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, and Tailwind CSS for responsive, mobile-friendly UI design.
  • Mapping & Geospatial APIs: Google Maps JavaScript API (Hybrid Satellite View, Geocoding, and Interactive Coordinate Pinning).
  • Earth Observation & Climate Data Sources:
    • NASA POWER API: Solar radiation, temperature extremes, humidity, and agroclimatology parameters.
    • NASA Earthdata / CMR Streams: GLDAS/NLDAS root-zone soil moisture, GPM IMERG precipitation reliability, MODIS/VIIRS/HLS vegetation indices (NDVI/EVI), ECOSTRESS thermal stress, and SRTM digital elevation/slope data.
    • SSURGO / Soil Lab Modeling: Soil texture, pH, organic matter, and NPK nutrient diagnostics.
  • Icons, Build & Deployment Stack: Lucide React iconography, Vite bundler, StackBlitz cloud IDE, GitHub version control, and Vercel / Netlify static hosting.
  • Hardware Requirements: Designed as a lightweight cloud web application requiring only a standard smartphone, tablet, or desktop browser with internet access—no specialized on-farm IoT sensors or high-end computing hardware needed.

What Makes the Project Creative

  • Multi-Season Systems Thinking Over Single-Crop Guessing: Most agricultural apps only recommend a single crop for the current season. AgroAdapt AI models 3-season agronomic synergy, scoring how one harvest prepares the soil and breaks pest cycles for the next.
  • Telemetry-to-Plain-Language Translation: Instead of overwhelming farmers with raw satellite bands or statistical charts, the platform frames complex datasets around intuitive, real-world questions (e.g., "Is my soil holding enough moisture?" or "Will heat stress hurt flowering?").
  • Live "What-If" Rotation Sandbox: Combining a bold, centerpiece Match Score with interactive crop-swapping cards turns complex agronomic modeling into an intuitive, tactile planning experience.

Factors Considered by the Team

  • Farmer Usability & Low Cognitive Load: Designed a streamlined, minimal-text interface with clear visual hierarchy, icon-driven navigation, and step-by-step guidance so users with varying levels of technical literacy can navigate effortlessly.
  • Data Reliability & Graceful Fallbacks: Accounted for intermittent rural connectivity and API rate limits by structuring resilient data pipelines that combine live satellite feeds with localized baseline models.
  • Global & Regional Adaptability: Incorporated multi-currency conversion (USD, INR, EUR, JPY), diverse soil profiles, and rainfed vs. irrigated farm configurations so the tool works equally well for a smallholder plot in India or a commercial farm abroad.
  • Environmental & Economic Balance: Weighted both immediate net profit and long-term ecological indicators (nitrogen balance, erosion control, and water conservation) so short-term yield gains do not come at the expense of soil degradation.
